recommended_first_journey.rationale: Personal Current Account Opening establishes the Customer aggregate root and the Account entity that the majority of subsequent retail journeys (JRN-002, JRN-006, JRN-011, JRN-016, JRN-026) depend on. It also exercises the KYC/AML onboarding path (CAP-005.01) and the Customer Onboarding Service (SVC-050, T1), which is a T1 compliance prerequisite in the service dependency map. Modelling this journey first ensures the event-storming workshop produces the CustomerOnboarded, KYCClearanceGranted, and AccountOpened domain events that anchor all downstream journey models.

journeys.name: Personal Current Account Opening
journeys.description: A personal customer applies for and successfully opens a personal current account, including digital KYC identity verification and initial CDD risk scoring. This is the foundational journey that establishes the Customer and Account aggregate roots used by all downstream retail journeys. It is mandated by the bank's PRA deposit-taking permission and the MLR 2017 CDD obligation at onboarding.
journeys.priority_rationale: MLR 2017 Regulation 27 mandates CDD before establishing a customer relationship. The Customer Onboarding Service (SVC-050) is a T1 compliance prerequisite in the service-dependencies tier model — no account provisioning can occur without it. This journey must be modelled first as it creates the Customer and Account entities used by JRN-002, JRN-006, JRN-011, JRN-016, JRN-026, and all other retail journeys.
journeys.happy_path_summary: 1. Customer initiates account opening via mobile app. 2. Bank requests identity documents; Onfido/Jumio biometric verification completes. 3. ComplyAdvantage PEP/sanctions screening returns CLEAR. 4. Customer risk score assigned (Low). 5. KYCClearanceGranted event published. 6. Account provisioned on Retail Banking Core (SVC-001); AccountOpened event published. 7. Debit card issued; welcome communications sent. 8. Customer authenticates and sees live account balance.

journeys.name: Faster Payment Initiation
journeys.description: A personal customer initiates a Faster Payment (FPS) from their current account to a third-party payee, including Confirmation of Payee check, real-time sanctions screening, and fraud scoring. This is a core statutory payment service under the Payment Services Regulations 2017 and the primary domestic payment rail. APP fraud reimbursement liability (PSR PS23/3, mandatory October 2024) makes this journey a regulatory priority.
journeys.priority_rationale: PSR SD17 mandates Confirmation of Payee on all outbound FPS payments. PSR PS23/3 (APP Fraud Reimbursement, in force October 2024) creates direct financial liability for the bank if this journey lacks fraud detection. The Fraud Detection Service (SVC-013) and Sanctions Screening Service (SVC-051) are both T1 prerequisites in the service dependency map, and FPS payment processing (SVC-009) has hard dependencies on both. Cannot be modelled without the Account entity established in JRN-001.
journeys.happy_path_summary: 1. Customer enters payee details in mobile app. 2. Confirmation of Payee check performed against payee sort code/account number. 3. Sanctions screening (SVC-051) confirms CLEAR on beneficiary. 4. Fraud Detection Service (SVC-013) scores payment; risk below threshold. 5. Customer authenticates via SCA (biometric). 6. Payment instruction submitted to FPS rail via SVC-009. 7. Vocalink routes to receiving bank; settlement confirmed. 8. PaymentSettled event published; push notification sent to customer.

journeys.name: SAR Filing by MLRO
journeys.description: The MLRO receives an internal suspicious activity disclosure from a member of staff, assesses it, and files a Suspicious Activity Report (SAR) with the NCA UKFIU within the statutory 5 business day window. This journey is a direct obligation under POCA 2002 s330 (failure to disclose) and MLR 2017, and carries personal criminal liability for the MLRO if not completed correctly.
journeys.priority_rationale: POCA 2002 s330 creates a criminal offence for failure to disclose knowledge or suspicion of money laundering. The MLRO (SMF17) has personal liability. The NCA UKFIU annual report 2023 highlighted SAR quality as under active supervisory scrutiny. KYC/AML Service (SVC-014) is T1 in the service dependency map. This journey is a standalone compliance obligation independent of customer-facing journeys but must be modelled early to define the SAR domain events and the MLRO case management workflow.
journeys.happy_path_summary: 1. Staff member submits internal disclosure to MLRO via secure case management system. 2. MLRO reviews transaction history and customer risk profile from KYC/AML Service (SVC-014). 3. MLRO determines suspicion is reasonable; tipping-off moratorium applied to customer communications. 4. SAR drafted using NCA UKFIU reporting format. 5. SAR submitted electronically to NCA UKFIU via SARs Online within 5 business days. 6. NCA acknowledgement received; SARRef recorded in case management. 7. Audit trail immutably logged (SVC-111). 8. MLRO annual report counter incremented.

journeys.name: Business Current Account Opening
journeys.description: An SME customer applies for and opens a business current account, including Know Your Business (KYB) checks, beneficial ownership determination, and enhanced due diligence for higher-risk structures. This journey establishes the BusinessCustomer and BusinessAccount entities that business lending, trade finance, and merchant services journeys depend on. Subject to MLR 2017 CDD/EDD requirements and FCA BCA switching obligations.
journeys.priority_rationale: MLR 2017 Regulation 28 requires enhanced CDD for corporate structures with complex beneficial ownership. The Customer Onboarding Service (SVC-050) async EDD path is specifically designed for this journey. Establishes the BusinessCustomer and BusinessAccount entities that JRN-007 (Business Loan Origination), JRN-013 (Trade Finance LC), JRN-023 (Merchant Onboarding), and JRN-014 (International Wire Transfer) all depend on. FCA BCA switching review (2025/26) makes this journey a near-term regulatory priority.
journeys.happy_path_summary: 1. Business owner initiates online account application for limited company. 2. Companies House API lookup confirms registered entity, directors, and PSCs. 3. Encompass automated KYB report generated; beneficial ownership confirmed. 4. Sanctions screening on all beneficial owners (>25% threshold) returns CLEAR. 5. CDD risk assessment completed; EDD not triggered (standard risk). 6. Business risk score assigned; KYCClearanceGranted published. 7. Business account provisioned on Commercial Banking Core (SVC-005). 8. BACS/FPS/CHAPS access enabled; online banking credentials issued.

journeys.name: APP Fraud Detection and Reimbursement
journeys.description: A fraud analyst investigates an Authorised Push Payment (APP) fraud claim submitted by a personal customer, determines eligibility under the PSR mandatory reimbursement scheme, and processes reimbursement up to £85,000 within the 5-business-day SLA. This journey is mandated by PSR PS23/3 (in force October 2024) and creates direct financial liability for the sending and receiving PSPs on a 50/50 split basis.
journeys.priority_rationale: PSR PS23/3 mandates reimbursement within 5 business days for eligible APP fraud claims up to £85,000, with costs split 50/50 between sending and receiving PSP. Non-compliance is subject to PSR enforcement under the Payment Systems Act 2013. FCA Consumer Duty consumer support outcome requires the bank not to deter customers from claiming. This is the highest-profile payment regulation enforcement focus in the PSR's current programme.
journeys.happy_path_summary: 1. Customer reports APP fraud via mobile app or telephone to Customer Service Agent. 2. Claim logged; fraud alert raised on originating payment. 3. Fraud Analyst retrieves original payment record from FPS rail data. 4. Fraud Detection Service (SVC-013) confirms payment was flagged as elevated risk at execution but customer overrode warning. 5. Analyst assesses customer claim against PSR eligibility criteria (no gross negligence, no professional fraud). 6. Reimbursement approved; debit to bank's APP fraud loss account. 7. Credit applied to customer account within 5 business days. 8. 50% recovery claim submitted to receiving PSP via Pay.UK reimbursement mechanism. 9. Case closed; regulatory reporting counter updated.

journeys.name: Residential Mortgage Application
journeys.description: A mortgage applicant applies for a residential mortgage through the bank's digital channel, receives an Agreement in Principle, submits a full application, and progresses through underwriting to mortgage offer. This journey exercises the Mortgages sub-capability (CAP-001.04, promoted to standalone) alongside Credit Risk (CAP-004.01) and is governed by MCOB affordability rules and the PRA stress rate test.
journeys.priority_rationale: Mortgages are the single largest consumer credit product by value in the UK. MCOB 11 affordability rules require documented stress-tested assessment. The bank's Mortgage Underwriter (PER-055) is an SM&CR Certified Function holder. Residential mortgage completions drive Material revenue and the mortgage application journey is the primary interaction point for the PER-005 persona segment (c. 800,000 UK completions annually).
journeys.happy_path_summary: 1. Applicant enters income, expenditure, and property details in digital AIP tool. 2. Automated credit bureau check (Experian); AIP issued within 60 seconds. 3. Full application submitted with income evidence (payslips, P60). 4. Mortgage Underwriter receives case; applies PRA stress rate affordability assessment. 5. Valuation instruction sent to RICS surveyor panel. 6. Surveyor completes desktop/physical valuation; report returned. 7. Underwriter approves subject to standard conditions; formal Mortgage Offer issued. 8. Customer's solicitor instructed; exchange and completion proceed. 9. Funds released via CHAPS on completion day. 10. Mortgage account created; first direct debit scheduled.

journeys.name: Business Loan Origination (SME Term Loan)
journeys.description: An SME customer applies for a term loan via their Relationship Manager. The RM originates the deal in the commercial lending system, a Credit Analyst prepares a credit paper, and the credit committee approves within the bank's Basel 3.1-compliant credit framework. This is the primary NIM-generating activity of the commercial bank.
journeys.priority_rationale: Business lending generates the bank's primary net interest margin. Basel 3.1 (PRA PS17/23, phased 2025–2030) raises RWA requirements for commercial lending, making capital-efficient origination workflows critical. The FCA SME lending review (FS23/3) is expected to impose new affordability and transparency requirements. OakNorth, Allica, and iwoca are taking share with faster digital decisioning, making this journey a competitive priority.
journeys.happy_path_summary: 1. RM creates loan opportunity in CRM (nCino). 2. SME submits management accounts, Open Banking data feed (Codat), and Companies House profile. 3. Credit Analyst builds financial model; stress-tests repayment under base-minus-200bp scenario. 4. Credit paper submitted to credit committee with RM recommendation. 5. Committee approves within delegated authority; credit limit set. 6. Legal documentation prepared; facility letter issued. 7. Customer signs; security perfected (fixed/floating charge registered at Companies House). 8. Drawdown instruction processed; loan proceeds credited to business current account. 9. Repayment direct debit schedule established. 10. Covenant monitoring programme activated.

journeys.name: Credit Card Application and Issuance
journeys.description: A personal customer applies for a personal credit card through the bank's digital channel, receives an instant credit decision, and is issued a virtual and physical card. The journey exercises the Credit Cards sub-capability (CAP-001.05, promoted to standalone), credit risk decisioning (CAP-004.01), and card processing (CAP-003.05). Governed by Consumer Credit Act 1974 and FCA CONC.
journeys.priority_rationale: Credit cards are the primary revolving credit product. CCA 1974 Section 75 joint and several liability creates a direct financial obligation on the bank. PCI DSS v4.0 compliance is mandatory for card issuance. The PSR cross-border interchange cap and Visa/Mastercard competition scrutiny create a changing revenue environment requiring a well-modelled card journey to inform commercial architecture decisions.
journeys.happy_path_summary: 1. Customer selects credit card product in mobile app. 2. Pre-filled application using existing customer KYC data (no re-KYC needed). 3. Credit bureau check (Experian); automated scorecard returns APPROVE. 4. Credit limit set by risk engine; regulated credit agreement disclosure presented. 5. Customer accepts terms electronically (compliant CCA 1974 signature). 6. Virtual card issued immediately; physical card dispatched within 3 working days. 7. Card number and CVV provisioned to Apple/Google Pay. 8. BIN management updated in card processing platform (GPS/Marqeta). 9. First monthly statement date scheduled.

journeys.name: International Wire Transfer (Corporate)
journeys.description: A corporate client (PER-002) instructs an international SWIFT payment from their BusinessAccount via the corporate banking portal or host-to-host API. The journey crosses CAP-003 (International Payments SVC-010), CAP-002 (Commercial Banking — account debit SVC-005), CAP-005 (Compliance — sanctions screening SVC-051), and CAP-004 (Risk Management — fraud SVC-013). ISO 20022 pacs.008 MX format is mandatory following the SWIFT CBPR+ MT coexistence period end (22 November 2025). SWIFT gpi tracking provides end-to-end visibility. Modelled artefacts: 6 phases (PH-029 to PH-034), 4 new entities (ENT-026 to ENT-029), 9 events (EVT-049 to EVT-057), new service SVC-010.
journeys.priority_rationale: SWIFT CBPR+ ISO 20022 mandatory from November 2025. CHAPS structured addresses from November 2026. UK FTR 2017 travel rule on all payments above €1,000. International payments are the highest FX revenue per transaction and face acute competitive pressure from Wise (sub-20bps) and Airwallex.
journeys.happy_path_summary: 1. PER-002 initiates cross-currency international wire via corporate portal (SVC-017). 2. BIC validated; SCA completed. 3. FX quotation obtained and accepted (PH-030). 4. Sanctions screening (SVC-051) and fraud scoring (SVC-013) run concurrently — both clear (PH-031). 5. pacs.008 assembled with UETR and LEI (PH-032). 6. SWIFT message submitted via SAA Cloud; BusinessAccount debited (PH-033). 7. Correspondent bank acknowledges via gpi ACSP. 8. Beneficiary bank credits beneficiary; gpi ACCC received. 9. TransferCompleted (EVT-056) published; PER-002 notified; WORM audit archived (PH-034).

journeys.name: Open Banking Consent and Payment Initiation
journeys.description: A Third Party Provider (PISP) requests payment initiation from a personal customer's account following explicit consent grant via the bank's Open Banking API. This journey exercises the Open Banking Payments sub-capability (CAP-003.06) and the Open Banking APIs sub-capability (CAP-007.03). Governed by PSR 2017, CMA Open Banking Order, and OBIE standards.
journeys.priority_rationale: CMA Open Banking Order mandates the bank provides premium API access to FCA-authorised TPPs without unnecessary obstacles. OBIE v3.1.x compliance is a live regulatory obligation. PSR SD17 (Confirmation of Payee) extends to open banking-initiated FPS payments. Commercial VRP (cVRP) launches Q1 2026, making this journey the foundation for a growing A2A payment revenue model that competes with card acquiring.
journeys.happy_path_summary: 1. Customer redirects from TPP (e.g. TrueLayer) to bank's consent portal. 2. Bank authenticates customer via SCA (app-based push notification). 3. Customer reviews and grants payment consent for specific amount and payee. 4. Consent token issued; customer redirected back to TPP. 5. TPP calls payment initiation endpoint with consent token. 6. API Gateway (SVC-101) validates TPP certificate and consent. 7. Sanctions screening and fraud scoring performed. 8. FPS payment submitted; PaymentInitiated event published. 9. Confirmation of funds response returned to TPP. 10. Push notification sent to customer confirming payment.

journeys.name: Card Transaction Authorisation
journeys.description: A personal customer makes a card-present or card-not-present purchase; the bank as card issuer receives the authorisation request from the card network, performs real-time fraud scoring and sanctions check, and responds with an authorisation or decline decision within the Visa/Mastercard sub-second SLA. This is a high-volume, real-time journey exercising CAP-003.05 (Card Processing, promoted to standalone).
journeys.priority_rationale: Card authorisation is a real-time service with a sub-second SLA mandated by Visa/Mastercard scheme rules. Authorisation failure is a direct customer experience failure that triggers switching. PCI DSS v4.0 scopes all cardholder data handled during authorisation. The PSR cross-border interchange cap makes revenue optimisation on this journey commercially important. PRA SS1/21 impact tolerance for card services requires this journey to be modelled before operational resilience self-assessment.
journeys.happy_path_summary: 1. Cardholder presents card at POS or enters card details online. 2. Merchant/acquirer sends ISO 8583 authorisation request to card network. 3. Visa/Mastercard routes to bank as card issuer. 4. Card Processing Service (SVC-011) validates BIN, card status, and available balance. 5. Fraud Detection Service (SVC-013) scores transaction; risk below threshold. 6. Sanctions check on merchant category (OFAC SDN merchant screening). 7. Authorisation response AUTH (approved) returned to network within SLA. 8. Hold placed on customer account balance. 9. Clearing and settlement processed T+1 via card scheme batch.

journeys.name: Direct Debit Setup and First Collection
journeys.description: A personal customer authorises a Direct Debit mandate for a utility or subscription provider. The bank registers the mandate via AUDDIS, and processes the first BACS collection including DDIC indemnity claim rights disclosure. This exercises the BACS Processing sub-capability (CAP-003.02) and the Current Accounts sub-capability (CAP-001.01).
journeys.priority_rationale: BACS processes over 6 billion Direct Debit and credit transactions annually; it is the primary mechanism for recurring payments including payroll, utility, and mortgage repayments. The bank as payer's PSP holds DDIC liability. Consumer Duty consumer support obligations require clear mandate management. Pay.UK BACS participation rules are an active scheme obligation.
journeys.happy_path_summary: 1. Customer completes Direct Debit instruction online or at point of service. 2. Originator submits AUDDIS new instruction file to BACS. 3. Bank validates account details; mandate registered in AUDDIS database. 4. Advance notice sent to customer (minimum 10 working days before first collection). 5. Collection file received 3 working days before value date. 6. BACS collection processed; funds debited from customer account on value date. 7. Payment confirmation posted to account statement. 8. DDIC rights communicated to customer; mandate visible in online banking mandate manager.

journeys.name: Trade Finance Letter of Credit Issuance
journeys.description: A corporate import client instructs the bank to issue a documentary Letter of Credit in favour of an overseas exporter. The bank as issuing bank creates the LC under UCP 600, routes it via SWIFT MT700 series (or ISO 20022 equivalent), and manages the document examination and payment obligation. This exercises the Trade Finance sub-capability (CAP-002.03, promoted to standalone). Enabled by the Electronic Trade Documents Act 2023.
journeys.priority_rationale: Trade Finance is a promoted capability (CAP-002.03, 4/4 promotion criteria) with high fee density per transaction. The Electronic Trade Documents Act 2023 (in force September 2023) creates a mandatory digital document programme. ICC UCP 600 and URDG 758 create structured legal obligations. ETDA 2023 compliance is a current regulatory obligation affecting all trade finance document workflows.
journeys.happy_path_summary: 1. Corporate RM submits LC application with trade contract details on trade finance platform (Finastra Trade Innovation). 2. Credit limit check against customer's trade finance facility. 3. Sanctions screening on beneficiary exporter and country of origin. 4. LC application reviewed and approved by trade finance operations. 5. SWIFT MT700 (or ISO 20022 fiti.013) issued to advising bank. 6. Advising bank notifies exporter; goods shipped; documents prepared. 7. Documents presented to bank; 5-day UCP 600 examination period. 8. Documents compliant; bank honours payment obligation to exporter. 9. Customer debited for LC face value plus fees. 10. Trade finance facility drawdown recorded.

journeys.name: FX Spot Trade Execution (Corporate)
journeys.description: A corporate client executes a spot FX trade via the bank's treasury portal or via their RM, converting a currency amount at a quoted rate for same-day or next-business-day settlement. This exercises the Treasury Services sub-capability (CAP-002.04, promoted to standalone) and the International Payments sub-capability (CAP-003.04). Governed by UK MiFIR best execution obligations for investment firms.
journeys.priority_rationale: FX spread income is the second-largest payment operations revenue stream. Fintech FX compression (Wise sub-20bps vs bank 80-150bps) is the most acute competitive pressure on commercial banking revenue. UK MiFIR best execution obligations apply to FX transactions for MiFID clients. The Treasury Dealer (PER-053) is an FCA-certified individual for dealing in investments as principal.
journeys.happy_path_summary: 1. Corporate treasurer requests GBP/USD spot rate via treasury portal. 2. Bank's treasury system fetches interbank rate from Bloomberg FXGO/ECN. 3. Mark-up applied per client tier; indicative rate displayed with 30-second validity window. 4. Customer confirms trade. 5. Trade booked in FX system; confirmation sent. 6. Settlement instruction generated for both legs (GBP debit, USD credit). 7. USD nostro account credited; GBP account debited. 8. SWIFT confirmation sent to corporate. 9. FX trade reported to FCA trade repository (UK MiFIR obligation). 10. FX margin crystallised in P&L.

journeys.name: HNW Investment Portfolio Review
journeys.description: A Wealth Advisor conducts an annual suitability review for a High Net Worth client, reassesses their risk profile and investment objectives, and recommends portfolio rebalancing. This exercises the Investment Advisory (CAP-006.01), Portfolio Management (CAP-006.02), and Private Banking (CAP-006.03) sub-capabilities. Governed by MiFID II COBS 9A suitability rules and Consumer Duty fair value obligations.
journeys.priority_rationale: MiFID II Article 54 requires annual suitability reports for clients with ongoing portfolio management arrangements. Consumer Duty price/value outcome requires evidence of fair value for wealth clients. Wealth Advisor (PER-057) is an SM&CR Certified Function holder. RM attrition risk (30-40% of book at risk per departure) makes the portfolio review journey a critical retention touchpoint.
journeys.happy_path_summary: 1. Advisor schedules annual review; client receives invitation via secure messaging. 2. Updated risk questionnaire completed by client; capacity for loss and knowledge assessed. 3. Advisor reviews current portfolio performance against benchmark. 4. Suitability assessment confirms profile unchanged; rebalancing recommended to reduce equity concentration. 5. Trade instructions generated for rebalancing; best execution policy applied. 6. Trades executed via FNZ custody platform. 7. Formal suitability letter issued to client with rationale. 8. Updated portfolio visible in online wealth portal. 9. Consumer Duty outcome evidence logged.

journeys.name: Overdraft Facility Review and Renewal
journeys.description: A retail customer's authorised overdraft facility reaches its annual review date; the bank's automated system reassesses affordability and credit risk, and either renews, modifies, or withdraws the facility. The bank must comply with FCA CONC persistent debt rules and Consumer Duty obligations on overdraft pricing and transparency.
journeys.priority_rationale: FCA CONC 6.7 persistent debt rules require the bank to identify customers paying more in interest and charges than principal over 18 months and take remedial action. FCA overdraft pricing reforms (PS19/16) require a single APR. Consumer Duty price/value outcome is under active FCA supervisory scrutiny for overdraft products. Overdraft revenue is material but declining post-2020 reforms.
journeys.happy_path_summary: 1. Automated review triggered 30 days before facility expiry. 2. Credit bureau refresh and account behaviour analysis (average balance, missed payments). 3. Affordability model re-run; facility renewed at same limit and APR. 4. Customer notified via app notification and email: facility renewed. 5. No action required from customer. 6. Persistent debt screening: customer not in persistent debt. 7. Renewed facility terms recorded; Consumer Duty outcome evidence saved.

journeys.name: Regulatory Return Submission (COREP Capital)
journeys.description: The bank's Regulatory Reporting team produces, validates, and submits a COREP capital adequacy return to the PRA on the prescribed quarterly schedule. This exercises the Regulatory Reporting sub-capability (CAP-005.02) and requires data inputs from the Risk Management capability (CAP-004). The CFO (SMF2) holds personal accountability for the accuracy of the submission.
journeys.priority_rationale: CRR UK Part Eight requires quarterly COREP submission on a fixed regulatory calendar. PRA PS17/23 (Basel 3.1) introduces new RWA calculation methodologies from January 2025, requiring updated reporting templates. Failure to submit on time or with materially inaccurate data exposes the bank to PRA enforcement. The PRA's modernising regulatory returns programme (CP4/24) signals ongoing change to reporting formats.
journeys.happy_path_summary: 1. Reporting calendar trigger initiates COREP extraction workflow. 2. RWA calculation engine (SVC-012) produces credit, market, and operational risk outputs. 3. AxiomSL/Wolters Kluwer regulatory reporting platform assembles COREP templates (C01.00 to C47.00). 4. Senior Risk and Finance reviewers validate key metrics against prior quarter movements. 5. CFO and CRO formally sign off return in governance system. 6. Return submitted to PRA via Gabriel/RegData portal. 7. PRA acknowledgement received and stored. 8. Restatement log updated (nil restatement this quarter).

journeys.name: Merchant Onboarding
journeys.description: An SME merchant customer applies to the bank for card acquiring services, including credit risk assessment for chargeback exposure, PCI DSS compliance assessment, and terminal provisioning. This exercises the Merchant Services sub-capability (CAP-002.05, promoted to standalone). Governed by PSR MR22/1.7 remedies and Visa/Mastercard scheme rules.
journeys.priority_rationale: Merchant acquiring is a promoted capability (CAP-002.05, 4/4 criteria) with a distinct regulatory regime (PSR MR22/1.7, PCI DSS). The PSR card acquiring market review (2023-2024) required enhanced pricing transparency remedies, making the onboarding journey a compliance target. Adyen and Stripe are capturing merchant origination; the bank's onboarding experience is a key competitive differentiator.
journeys.happy_path_summary: 1. SME applies for merchant acquiring via online portal or RM referral. 2. KYB checks confirm legitimate business; beneficial ownership verified. 3. Merchant category code (MCC) risk assessment: standard retail (low chargeback risk). 4. Credit risk assessment for chargeback exposure: approved. 5. PCI DSS compliance questionnaire completed; SAQ-A for card-not-present. 6. Worldpay/Fiserv bureau processor notified; MID assigned. 7. Terminal(s) dispatched; payment gateway credentials issued. 8. Test transaction processed; settlement confirmed. 9. MDR pricing communicated per PSR transparency requirements.

journeys.name: Customer Complaint Handling
journeys.description: A personal or SME customer lodges a formal complaint about a bank product or service. The bank acknowledges within 24 hours, investigates, and resolves within 8 weeks under FCA DISP rules. Consumer Duty consumer support outcome requires the complaint process not to deter customers or impose unreasonable barriers.
journeys.priority_rationale: FCA DISP rules mandate complaint acknowledgement within 24 hours and resolution within 8 weeks. Consumer Duty consumer support outcome is a live FCA supervisory priority. FOS uphold rates are a reputational metric monitored by the FCA and published annually. Unresolved complaints are the primary driver of FOS escalation and regulatory intervention under the Consumer Duty supervisory programme.
journeys.happy_path_summary: 1. Customer submits complaint via app secure messaging or telephone. 2. Complaint logged in case management system; acknowledgement sent within 24 hours. 3. Case assigned to Customer Service Agent; root cause investigation initiated. 4. If payment-related, FPS/CHAPS transaction records retrieved. 5. Decision made: upheld (goodwill payment or redress calculated) or not upheld (rationale documented). 6. Final response letter issued within 8 weeks. 7. Consumer Duty evidence trail saved. 8. Root cause data fed into product governance team for systemic issue monitoring.

journeys.name: CDD Periodic Review (Corporate)
journeys.description: The compliance function triggers a periodic CDD review for an existing corporate client on a risk-based schedule. An automated pKYC event (Companies House filing, adverse media alert) or a scheduled 3-year review prompts the review. The MLRO team verifies continued beneficial ownership accuracy, re-screens against sanctions lists, and updates the client risk score.
journeys.priority_rationale: MLR 2017 Regulation 28 requires ongoing CDD monitoring on a risk-based basis. FCA/JMLSG guidance is moving toward event-triggered perpetual KYC (pKYC) replacing fixed-cycle review. The FCA's enforcement focus (Starling Bank £29m fine, October 2024) specifically targeted incomplete screening coverage. OFSI expects beneficial ownership screening through corporate structures as standard.
journeys.happy_path_summary: 1. Encompass automated alert: director change filed at Companies House. 2. pKYC trigger published; case created in KYC/AML case management (SVC-014). 3. Analyst re-runs beneficial ownership lookup; new director identified. 4. Sanctions screening on new director: CLEAR. 5. Adverse media check: no negative results. 6. Updated client risk score calculated: unchanged (Medium). 7. RM notified; client not contacted unless risk escalation required. 8. Updated CDD record stored; next review date reset. 9. Audit trail updated in WORM store.

journeys.name: GDPR Data Subject Access Request
journeys.description: A personal customer submits a Subject Access Request (SAR) under UK GDPR Article 15. The bank's DPO team locates all personal data across systems, redacts third-party data, and provides a comprehensive response within the 30-day statutory deadline.
journeys.priority_rationale: UK GDPR Article 15 right of access requires response within 30 days. ICO enforcement in financial services is increasing; enforcement notices have been issued for failure to honour data subject rights on time. While operationally important, this journey does not generate revenue and is lower priority than regulatory payment and credit journeys. OneTrust SAR workflow tooling is the buy candidate.
journeys.happy_path_summary: 1. Customer submits SAR via online banking portal or post. 2. Identity verified (SCA for digital, document verification for postal). 3. SAR case created in OneTrust workflow; 30-day clock starts. 4. Automated data extraction queries Retail Banking Core, KYC records, transaction history, communications archive. 5. Legal team reviews; third-party data redacted. 6. Response pack compiled (PDF); encrypted delivery link issued to customer. 7. Response delivered within 30 days. 8. Case closed; ICO notification log updated (no breach).

journeys.name: Annual Stress Test Participation (PRA)
journeys.description: The bank participates in the PRA's annual concurrent stress test. The Risk team produces projected stressed balance sheet and P&L outputs under prescribed macroeconomic scenarios, submits to the PRA, and presents results to the Board Risk Committee. This exercises the Model Risk (CAP-004.05), Credit Risk (CAP-004.01), Market Risk (CAP-004.02) sub-capabilities and the Regulatory Reporting sub-capability (CAP-005.02).
journeys.priority_rationale: PRA concurrent stress tests are an annual regulatory submission obligation for banks above the PRA's size threshold. The output informs Pillar 2A capital buffer setting and may result in PRA capital add-ons. While mandatory, stress test modelling is an annual batch process with a defined regulatory calendar, making it lower priority than real-time transaction journeys for event-storming sequencing.
journeys.happy_path_summary: 1. PRA publishes stress test scenarios and data templates (typically Q1). 2. Risk Management team loads PRA macroeconomic scenarios into stress testing models. 3. Credit risk models project 3-year loan loss rates under severe adverse scenario. 4. Market risk models project FRTB losses under stress. 5. Operational risk adds Basel SA OpRisk capital. 6. Finance consolidates into projected stressed CET1 ratio trajectory. 7. Model Validation team signs off model outputs per SS1/23. 8. Board Risk Committee reviews and approves submission. 9. Data submitted to PRA via prescribed templates. 10. PRA feedback received; results incorporated into ICAAP.

journeys.name: Correspondent Bank Relationship Setup
journeys.description: The bank establishes a new nostro/vostro correspondent banking relationship with a foreign financial institution to facilitate international payment settlement in a new currency corridor. The process includes FATF Recommendation 13 enhanced due diligence, SWIFT BIC registration, and nostro account funding. Governed by MLR 2017 Regulation 34 (correspondent relationships).
journeys.priority_rationale: FATF Recommendation 13 and MLR 2017 Regulation 34 impose enhanced due diligence obligations on correspondent banking relationships, including senior management approval. De-risking of correspondent relationships (reduced global coverage, particularly in emerging markets) is an active regulatory concern. This is an infrequent operational journey that is lower priority than customer-facing journeys but must be modelled to define the CorrespondentOnboarded domain event.
journeys.happy_path_summary: 1. Treasury team identifies need for new currency corridor (e.g. KES corridor for East Africa payments). 2. SWIFT KYC Registry lookup confirms correspondent bank profile. 3. FATF R13 EDD conducted: regulatory status, AML controls, sanctions screening programme verified. 4. Senior Management approval obtained per MLR 2017 R34. 5. Correspondent banking agreement executed. 6. SWIFT relationship established; nostro account opened. 7. Test SWIFT message exchanged. 8. Correspondent relationship live; currency added to international payment matrix. 9. Annual EDD review scheduled.

journeys.name: Senior Manager Dashboard and SM&CR Accountability Review
journeys.description: The Head of Compliance (SMF16) conducts a quarterly review of SM&CR conduct rule compliance across the bank, reviews the accountability map, updates Statements of Responsibilities for role changes, and submits any breach reports to the FCA. This exercises the Conduct Monitoring sub-capability (CAP-005.03) and is a governance journey rather than a customer-facing journey.
journeys.priority_rationale: SM&CR conduct rules are a live FCA obligation for all banks. Breach of conduct rules by an SMF holder carries personal enforcement risk including financial penalties and industry prohibition. However, this is a governance review journey with a known quarterly cadence and limited domain event complexity — appropriate to model after higher-priority customer-facing journeys.
journeys.happy_path_summary: 1. Quarterly review triggered by compliance calendar. 2. Behavox/NICE Actimize Surveillance communications scan completed; no conduct alerts raised. 3. SM&CR accountability map reviewed for role changes; two new Certified Function individuals identified since last review. 4. FCA register updated for new CF holders. 5. Statements of Responsibilities reviewed; no material changes. 6. Annual conduct training completion rates verified: 98% compliance. 7. Board Compliance Report section updated. 8. No breach notifications required this quarter.

journeys.name: Branch Cash Management
journeys.description: Branch staff at a retail branch manage daily cash inventory — ordering from, and repatriating to, the bank's cash centre — and process customer cash deposits and withdrawals including AML cash reporting thresholds. This exercises the Current Accounts sub-capability (CAP-001.01) and Conduct Monitoring (CAP-005.03).
journeys.priority_rationale: Branch cash operations are a declining activity as digital substitution reduces cash transaction volumes (UK cash use below 15% of retail transactions in 2024). MLR 2017 Regulation 37 requires enhanced vigilance for cash deposits above £10,000. While the journey is a live operational obligation, it is low volume and declining, making it the lowest-priority modelling candidate. UK branch count has declined from ~9,000 to under 4,000 (2015–2024).
journeys.happy_path_summary: 1. Branch manager reviews overnight cash position report. 2. Cash order placed with GardaWorld/Brinks for next-day delivery if below minimum float. 3. Customer presents £12,000 cash deposit at counter. 4. Branch staff collect ID; AML cash threshold report generated (above £10,000). 5. Cash counted and verified via cash handling machine. 6. Deposit posted to customer account. 7. Transaction flagged to MLRO team for review per AML policy. 8. Cash vault reconciled at close of business. 9. Surplus cash repatriated to cash centre.

journeys.name: Personal Savings Account Opening and ISA Subscription
journeys.description: A personal customer opens a cash ISA and makes their annual subscription. This exercises the Savings & Deposits sub-capability (CAP-001.02) and requires HMRC ISA manager validation. The bank holds ISA manager obligations under HMRC Individual Savings Account Regulations 1998.
journeys.priority_rationale: Cash ISAs are a key retail deposit product with £350bn+ in the UK ISA market. FCA Consumer Duty requires fair value assessment of savings products; Dear CEO letters (2022-2024) specifically challenged banks on easy-access savings rates. HMRC ISA manager obligations include annual ISA return submission and subscription validation. Competitive pressure from Raisin and Flagstone deposit marketplaces requires a well-modelled savings journey.
journeys.happy_path_summary: 1. Customer selects Cash ISA in mobile app; annual allowance validated against HMRC ISA register. 2. ISA application pre-filled from existing KYC data; no additional identity check required. 3. Customer confirms ISA product terms and interest rate. 4. Cash ISA account opened; HMRC ISA manager notification submitted. 5. Customer transfers £20,000 (annual allowance) from current account. 6. Interest accrual commences; confirmation sent via push notification. 7. ISA account visible in portfolio overview alongside current account.

journeys.name: Personal Loan Application and Drawdown
journeys.description: A personal customer applies for an unsecured personal loan through the bank's digital channel and receives an instant credit decision via automated scorecard. On acceptance, funds are disbursed to the customer's current account. Governed by FCA CONC, Consumer Credit Act 1974 pre-contract disclosure requirements, and Consumer Duty fair value obligations.
journeys.priority_rationale: Unsecured personal lending is a core retail revenue product. Consumer Credit Act 1974 Section 61 requires a regulated credit agreement before drawdown. CONC affordability rules require creditworthiness assessment. FCA persistent debt rules (CONC 6.7) apply from 18 months after loan origination if in persistent debt. BNPL regulation (expected 2025-2026) will create a level playing field that may affect pricing strategy.
journeys.happy_path_summary: 1. Customer accesses pre-approved loan offer in mobile app (triggered by salary credit pattern analysis). 2. Customer selects loan amount (£5,000) and term (36 months). 3. Soft credit check confirms no material change since pre-approval. 4. Regulated pre-contract information and credit agreement displayed. 5. Customer e-signs via in-app signature. 6. 14-day cooling-off period disclosed; loan proceeds released immediately. 7. £5,000 credited to current account via internal transfer. 8. First monthly repayment scheduled via direct debit. 9. Consumer Duty outcome evidence logged.

journeys.name: CHAPS High-Value Payment (Property Purchase)
journeys.description: A mortgage customer's solicitor requests a CHAPS payment on completion day to discharge the purchase price of a residential property. The bank processes the CHAPS instruction under the Bank of England RT2 settlement engine, applying ISO 20022 enhanced data requirements (LEI and structured address from May 2025). This is the highest-value single-payment event in the retail banking journey set.
journeys.priority_rationale: CHAPS ISO 20022 Enhanced Data Phase 1 (LEIs and Purpose Codes) is mandatory from 1 May 2025. Phase 2 (structured addresses) is mandatory from November 2026. CHAPS high-value settlement is an important business service under PRA SS1/21 with a zero-tolerance for outages. Property completion CHAPS payments are time-critical — a payment failure on completion day creates legal liability and regulatory exposure.
journeys.happy_path_summary: 1. Solicitor submits CHAPS instruction via secure banking portal on completion day. 2. Instruction received by bank's CHAPS processing team. 3. Sanctions screening on beneficiary (OFSI, OFAC) returns CLEAR. 4. ISO 20022 pacs.008 message constructed: structured beneficiary address, purpose code (PRCT — property purchase), originator LEI populated. 5. CHAPS submission window validated; instruction within cutoff. 6. Payment submitted to Bank of England RT2 RTGS settlement engine. 7. Settlement confirmed; funds irrevocably transferred to seller's bank. 8. CHAPS confirmation sent to solicitor and customer. 9. Mortgage charge registered at HM Land Registry.

journeys.name: Commercial VRP (Variable Recurring Payment) Consent Setup
journeys.description: A corporate or retail customer grants a Variable Recurring Payment (VRP) consent to a PISP/merchant under the FCA's commercial VRP (cVRP) scheme (first live payments expected Q1 2026). The bank processes the consent, enforces parameters (maximum amount, frequency, expiry), and processes subsequent VRP payments without per-payment SCA. This exercises the Open Banking Payments sub-capability (CAP-003.06) and Open Banking APIs (CAP-007.03).
journeys.priority_rationale: FCA cVRP scheme is expected to launch in Q1 2026 as a new open banking payment rail for subscription and sweeping use cases. PSR National Payments Vision explicitly supports A2A as an alternative to card recurring mandates. cVRP creates a new payment product that competes with Direct Debit and card recurring for merchant-side and consumer-side use cases. Early modelling is required to influence the API gateway architecture design (CAP-007.03 pending 2026 promotion review).
journeys.happy_path_summary: 1. Customer is redirected from merchant to bank's VRP consent portal. 2. Bank authenticates customer via SCA (biometric). 3. Customer reviews VRP parameters: max £500/month, subscription category, 12-month expiry. 4. VRP consent granted; consent ID issued to PISP. 5. First VRP payment instruction received from PISP with consent reference. 6. Bank validates: amount within consent parameters, frequency within limits, consent not expired. 7. Fraud scoring performed; within normal subscription pattern. 8. FPS payment executed; PaymentSettled event published. 9. Subsequent VRP payments processed without per-payment SCA until consent expires or is revoked.

journeys.name: Insurance Product Distribution (Packaged Account)
journeys.description: A retail customer upgrades to a packaged current account that includes travel insurance underwritten by a third-party insurer. The bank acts as insurance intermediary under ICOBS and FCA PROD, conducting a target market assessment and fair value check before distributing the insurance product. This exercises the Insurance Distribution sub-capability (CAP-001.06, promoted to standalone) and is a T4 service in the dependency map.
journeys.priority_rationale: Insurance Distribution (SVC-004) is a T4 service in the service dependency map — it is a revenue overlay that requires all T2/T3 core banking services to be operational first. ICOBS and IDD require fair value assessment before distribution. Consumer Duty PROD 4 (insurance product oversight and governance) is a live regulatory obligation. PPI mis-selling history (£38bn in redress) makes this journey a regulatory sensitivity area, but it is operationally lower priority than payment and credit journeys.
journeys.happy_path_summary: 1. Customer selects Premier Account upgrade in mobile app. 2. Insurance product target market assessment displayed: customer fits the identified target market (frequent traveller, aged 18-75). 3. Fair value assessment completed: insurance premium provides adequate cover relative to cost. 4. Key Features Document and IPID presented; customer accepts. 5. Insurance policy bound with underwriter (Aviva) via API. 6. Policy number issued; certificate of insurance sent via email. 7. Monthly fee updated on current account. 8. Consumer Duty evidence trail saved. 9. Customer can view and cancel insurance within the bank's app.
